US SUBSTANTIAL PRESENCE TEST CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Are you a US tax resident yet?

List your days in the United States. You get the 183-day weighted count (this year, plus a third of last year, plus a sixth of the year before), how many more days you can spend this year and stay under the test, the date you crossed it, and what a planned trip would do.

Your dates, not tax advice. Every value is editable and nothing is uploaded: dates are used in this browser tab only.

Your days in the United States

One stay per line, first and last day inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD. Any part of a day counts. Add exempt to a line for days that do not count (student, teacher, medical, crew, commuter, transit). Know only a year's total? Write 2024: 120 days.

Have your I-94 travel history?

At i94.cbp.dhs.gov, "Get Most Recent I-94", then "Travel History", lists every arrival and departure. Select the table, paste it here, and it turns into stays above. Matching and the arithmetic happen in this tab; the paste is never uploaded.

Common questions

What is the substantial presence test?

You are a US resident for tax purposes if you were in the US at least 31 days this year and the weighted total is at least 183: all your days this year, plus one third of your days last year, plus one sixth of your days the year before. Any part of a day counts as a day. On the sample dates 91 days this year, 120 last year and 120 the year before weigh 151.0, so 31 more days stay under the test.

Why can 120 days a year still make me a US resident?

Because earlier years count. 120 days each year weighs 120 + 40 + 20 = 180, just under 183; 123 days in the third year reaches 183. The calculator shows the most days you can spend this year and still stay under, given the two years before.

Which days do not count?

Days as an exempt individual (for example F-1 or J-1 students, teachers and trainees within the allowed years), days you could not leave because of a medical condition that began here, crew members, Canada or Mexico commuters, and transit stops under 24 hours. Mark such a stay exempt and it is left out of the count.

Is this tax advice?

No. It counts the days you type and nothing is uploaded. It does not decide whether you are an exempt individual, whether a treaty or the closer connection exception applies, or what you owe, and it is not a substitute for IRS Publication 519 or a qualified professional.

US Substantial Presence Test Calculator · guide

The substantial presence test: how the 183-day count works

Short answer: you are a US resident for tax purposes if you were here at least 31 days this year and this year's days, plus a third of last year's, plus a sixth of the year before's, add up to 183 or more. Staying 120 days a year is not safe: it weighs 180 in the third year and 183 after three more days.

Everything below is arithmetic on invented dates. Not tax, legal or immigration advice. Exempt-individual status, tax treaties, the closer connection exception (Form 8840) and the first-year choice can change what you owe. Check IRS Publication 519.

A worked example

Three-month client stints: 2023-03-01 to 2023-06-28, 2024-03-01 to 2024-06-28 and 2025-03-01 to 2025-05-30, as of 2025-06-15, with 40 more days planned in 2025.

  • Days present: 91 in 2025, 120 in 2024, 120 in 2023.
  • Weighted: 91 + 120 ÷ 3 + 120 ÷ 6 = 151.0, which is under 183.
  • The most days you can spend in 2025 and stay under the test is 122, so 31 more days are safe.
  • The planned 40 days make 131 days in 2025 and the weighted total reaches 183, so that trip meets the test.

How to keep your count honest

  • Count every day you were in the US for any part of the day, including the days you land and leave.
  • Leave out only days the rules exempt: days as an exempt individual (certain F, J, M and Q visa holders), a medical condition that began here, crew members, Canada or Mexico commuters and transit stops under 24 hours.
  • Plan around the year ahead: this year's days become a third of next year's count.
  • If you meet the test but were here fewer than 183 days this year, ask a preparer about the closer connection exception on Form 8840.

Common questions

How are the three years weighted?

All of the days you were present this year, one third of the days last year, and one sixth of the days the year before. You must also have been present at least 31 days this year. The total must reach 183.

Does a day I land or leave count?

Yes. Any part of a day in the US is a day present, the opposite of the 330-day FEIE test, where only full days abroad count.

Is this tax advice?

No. It is arithmetic on invented dates. Check IRS Publication 519 or a qualified professional. No warranty.
